digest.component_or_area: compaction sweep — crash-atomic fold with intent journal recovery
propositions: Detached compaction sweep worker that dies between snapshot write/retire and git commit leaves the tracker working tree dirty with tracked deletions and untracked snapshot files, causing the next reconverge to abort on local changes and strand ticket commits.

A detached sweep killed or racing a concurrent writer between rename and commit can leave the store in an inconsistent state with no automatic recovery, creating chronic wedges that require manual intervention.

An intent journal written before any mutations, ordered mutation steps (snapshot-write → renames → single commit), and startup-time recovery of abandoned folds can make the fold crash-atomic such that any kill leaves a clean tree on next sweep entry.

Recovery must discriminate three cases: journal with snapshot already in HEAD (discard journal only), journal with uncommitted snapshot (revert sources, remove snapshot, clear journal), and journal with missing snapshot (clear journal without touching files), while deferring on transient git failures to avoid mis-reverting a landed fold.
Incomplete rollback that fails mid-reverse-rename must retain the uncommitted snapshot as SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT for fsck repair rather than delete it and lose folded events.
Sweep must commit each fold individually within its own locked section and run recovery as a preamble, so a killed sweep leaves zero dirty folds and the store converges to clean on next entry.
